methodology.description: Each session is a completely separate Node process (different PID), invoked via 'npx tsx scripts/phase-4c-a2-single-session.ts <N>'. Each process creates a fresh MCP server, scans the same immutable Kestrel target, and writes results to a session-specific JSON file.
methodology.processIsolation: Full process lifecycle — no shared state between sessions
methodology.semgrepIsolation: Each session spawns its own Semgrep child process

historicalAnomaly.description: A prior C2R full forensics run produced 859 raw matches and 798 actionable findings (vs current 898/833). That run had 136 parser errors (vs current ~101). The higher parser error count caused fewer files to be successfully parsed, resulting in fewer findings.
historicalAnomaly.rootCause: SEMGREP_PARSER_STATE — Semgrep's parser non-deterministically fails on different numbers of files across sessions. The C2R run had 35 more parser errors, causing 39 fewer raw matches.
historicalAnomaly.impact: Finding population CAN vary across sessions when parser error count changes significantly. However, 3 consecutive independent processes in this test produced identical results.
historicalAnomaly.stabilityAssessment: Stable within a session cluster, but occasional outliers with higher parser error rates have been observed historically.

conclusion: PASS_WITH_DOCUMENTED_LIMITATION — All 3 independent processes produced identical semantic results (findingSetDigest, concernFamilySetDigest, rawEngineMatches, actionableFindingInstances, verdict, completeness). filesSkippedByEngine varies by ±1 (ENGINE_OPERATIONAL_NONDETERMINISM). A historical anomaly (C2R: 859/798 vs current: 898/833) was investigated and classified as SEMGREP_PARSER_STATE — the C2R run had 136 parser errors vs current ~101, causing fewer files to be parsed and fewer findings. This is a Semgrep engine limitation, not an HAIEC adapter issue.
recommendation: A. Semgrep execution can potentially be hardened with --jobs 1 (single-worker) to reduce parallelism-related parser state variation. B. The claim should be narrowed to acknowledge that Semgrep parser coverage may vary on parser-edge-case files.
